Histopathologic examination (Punch biopsy):     - Demonstrated viral changes to the epidermis with ballooning degeneration of keratinocytes with intracytoplasmic inclusions (Guarnieri bodies) and a brisk lymphocytic and neutrophilic infiltrate
PCR Test:    - Confirmed presence of vaccinia virus

Images:    Figure 1 Title: Clinical Findings    Description: Vesiculopustules with central umbilication in the beard area at time of presentation        Figure 2 Title: Histopathologic Findings From Lesional Skin of the Right Cheek    Description: Shows epidermal necrosis, intraepidermal edema, ballooning degeneration, necrotic keratinocytes, neutrophilic infiltrate, and Guarnieri bodies within keratinocytes.

bindings.label: 4-day history of progressive vesiculopustular eruption of the anterior neck and chin

Patient denied symptoms of pruritus, burning, or fever at time of presentation; had not received smallpox vaccination but had engaged in simulated unarmed combat with individuals who had recently been vaccinated

Physical examination revealed more than 2 dozen monomorphic, broad-based folliculocentric pustules with central umbilication, overlying serum crust, and surrounding erythema and edema of the anterior neck, chin, and inferior cheeks
During hospitalization, the patient developed fevers to 39°C, progressive edema of the face, and anterior cervical lymphadenopathy
Medical history was noncontributory, and the patient was not taking any medications
PCR assay detected vaccinia virus DNA in patient specimen
Electron microscopy revealed viral particles within Guarnieri bodies
Histopathology demonstrated Guarnieri bodies and viral inclusions
